The retrieved literature (hydrology, circuit models, ecology) has nothing to do with NAS-Bench-201, so these hypotheses come from the cell's graph structure and prior knowledge of the benchmark.

**8 common assumptions and their negations**

1. *Conv gains add up across edges.* If false, a conv gains less when a parallel path already has a strong op (hypotheses 29 and 30).
2. *Skip on the direct edge 3 helps by a fixed amount.* If false, its benefit depends on how many other routes reach the output (23, 24).
3. *Setting an edge to `none` always hurts.* If false, it is harmless when the edge is already disconnected by an upstream `none` (8-12).
4. *Replacing an op has the same effect whatever it replaces.* If false, upgrading from `none` gains more than upgrading from `skip`, and removing a good op costs more than removing a poor one (1-7, 13-15).
5. *Pooling is weak and unconditional.* If false, it helps mostly when it fills an empty slot (20, 21) and little when the edge already has `skip` (22).
6. *All edges are equivalent.* If false, the edges into the output (3, 4, 5) matter differently from the interior edges (16, 25-28).
7. *3x3 conv is uniformly better than 1x1.* If false, the gain from adding a conv depends on what the slot held before (17, 18).
8. *Edge effects are independent of connectivity.* If false, an edit on a dead-end edge has zero effect (8-12, 25-28).
